title: Sequence-aware GPU saturation + dependent-service hibernation chaos harness
creator: Laura Chen
description: Design and implement a targeted chaos harness that reproduces two realistic production pressure patterns: (1) sequence-length-correlated GPU saturation (long-sequence bursts from a small tenant subset) and (2) dependent-service hibernation (metadata / rate-limit store becomes slow/blackholed). The harness should exercise circuit-breaker rules, tiered load-shedding, and multi-region failover paths while producing traceable telemetry for SLO validation. Deliverables: reusable harness, Canary test suite, dashboards, runbook, and an automated experiment runner that can be invoked from CI or via the chaos dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can simulate per-tenant long-sequence bursts that increase GPU memory and KV cache pressure without requiring production traffic
Harness can induce and recover from simulated dependent-service blackholes (metadata-store and billing-lookup) with configurable latency/failure profiles
Circuit-breaker and load-shed responses observed match policy (requests rejected with proper http status and telemetry tags) and do not violate high-priority SLO targets for control-plane operations
Multi-region failover triggers when regional admission control trips and requests successfully route to fallback region with no more than configured failover RTO
Artifacts: reproducible experiment config, CI job to run smoke experiments, dashboard with token-latency/cost/SLO breakdown, and a documented runbook for on-call execution and rollback
steps: Prototype harness module in chaos-service that can target a region and tenant set (step functions + k8s job)
Add sequence profile generator: short/medium/long token distributions, controlled concurrency per tenant
Wire GPU pressure measurement hooks (per-pool memory, utilization, queue depth) and KV cache hit/miss metrics
Implement dependent-service sink: toggles for latency injection, TCP blackhole, and partial-error modes against metadata and rate-limit endpoints
Integrate with circuit-breaker controller: ensure test can flip breakers by simulating downstream error budgets
Create Canary experiment definitions for staged rollout: unit/harness CI -> staging cluster -> limited-production guardrail
Build dashboards and alert rules for experiment: per-tenant error rates, latency p50/p95/p99, failover counts, token-per-second, and cost delta
Author runbook with OODA-style steps, safe abort, and example mitigation commands (drain pool, pause chaos job, revert routing)
observability: Trace spans annotated with chaos.experiment_id and target_tenant
Event logs for circuit-breaker state transitions with policy id and triggered reason
Dashboards: SLO burn-down, failover sequence timeline, tenant impact heatmap, cost-per-token during experiment
rollout_plan: Dev run: 1 hour in isolated dev cluster (validate harness stability)
Staging run: night window, restrict to synthetic tenant set, low concurrency, check dashboards
Canary: single region production with strict abort if priority-0 SLO deviation > 0.5% over 5 minutes
Limited ramp: gradually increase tenant set and concurrency while monitoring failover and breaker metrics
Full abort criteria: increase in control-plane latency > 30ms, spike in P99 generation latency > 20%, or error-rate > configured threshold
risks: Accidentally overloading shared GPU pools causing broader customer impact if isolation is misconfigured
Dependent-service hibernation could trigger cascading circuit breaks in control plane components not covered by tests
False-positive SLO regressions due to missing telemetry tags or query-time aggregation errors
Rollback complexity if multi-region routing state is partially applied and experiment stopped mid-failover
